Haupts Definition seiner Geschlechtsidentität lautet: "Klar, man hat sich schwul zu verhalten." Auf eine noch kürzere Formel gebracht: Schwul sein, ohne Schwuchtel zu sein.
Haupt's definition of his gender identity is: "Sure, you have to act gay." Put even more succinctly: Being gay without being a sissy.
schwul.et:
Borrowed from Middle Low German swōl, swūl (“sultry, hot and humid”) (17th century), adopted into Standard German as schwül in the 18th century, ultimately from the root of schwelen (“to smoulder”).
The older form without umlaut appears in Berlin dialect in th…

s: male homosexual; faggot, fairy, fruit, poof, queen (homosexual)
Schwuchtel.et: Probably akin to or derived from regional schwuchteln (“to dance around; prance”).

s: Mit einem Schwung warf er alle Akten vom Tisch.
In one sweep he threw all the files off the desk.
a quantity so swept, (hence colloquial) any large amount
Sie knallte mir einen Schwung Akten auf den Tisch.
She banged a pile of files onto my desk.
momentum, speed, force (intensity of a specific movement)
Du musst mit mehr Schwung über die Rampe fahren, wenn du weiter springen willst.
You need to go over the ramp with more speed if you want to jump further.
Er soll die flaue Wirtschaft wieder in Schwung bringen.
His job is to stir the sagging economy.
Die Show wirkt altbacken, sie braucht wieder mehr Schwung.
The show feels stodgy, it needs to get some pep back.
Schwung.et: From Middle High German swunc, ablaut derivation from swingen, modern schwingen (“to swing”). Originally infrequent, but in general use since the 18th century.

Schwur.et: From Middle High German swuor, from Old High German swuor, from Proto-Germanic *swōraz (“oath”), from Proto-Germanic *swarjaną (“to speak, swear”). Compare English swear and Vilamovian śwür.

s: Es ist so schwül, so dumpfig hie, / Und ist doch eben so warm nicht drauß’.
It is so sultry, so humid here, / and yet it's not even that hot outside.
schwül.et: Borrowed from Low German, from Middle Low German swōl, swūl, in Standard German since the 18th century, ultimately from the root of schwelen (“to smoulder”). The umlaut is possibly due to analogy with kühl (“cool”). The unumlauted form schwul is limited to the…

schwülstig.et: Schwulst + -ig. Doublet of schwulstig, which has developed slightly different meanings. Compare Swedish svulstig.

s: swollen, puffy, bloated (as a result of an illness, infection, injury, etc.)
schwulstig.et: Schwulst + -ig. Doublet of schwülstig, which has developed slightly different meanings. Compare Swedish svulstig.

Schwulst.et: From Middle High German swulst f (“tumor, growth”), from swellen (“to swell up, bulge”), from Old High German swellan, ultimately from Proto-Germanic *swellaną (“to swell”).

s: Die Aufgabenstellung hat mich in beträchtliche Schwulitäten versetzt.
The task at hand was seriously troublesome for me.
„Es ist aber ein Menschenbedürfnis,“ sagte Wehsal kläglich, „ein Menschenbedürfnis, lieber Castorp, zu reden und sich das Herz zu erleichtern, wenn man in solchen Schwulitäten sitzt wie ich.“
“But it is a human need,” Wehsal said miserably “a human need, my dear Castorp, to talk and speak your heart, when you're in such trouble as I am.”
Schwulität.et: Jocular 18th c. student slang, from schwul, schwül (“hot”) + -ität.

Schwund.et: Early 19th century, analogical ablaut formation from the verb. Compare the participle geschwunden and deverbal nouns like Bruch, Bund, Fund, Sprung.

His appearance animated the party.

The rookie breathed new life into the team.

We've got to drum up some business in the shop.

The party has livened up.

Have I not kept my oath?

Have you forgotten your pledge?

It is so humid in summer here.

Hot and humid weather puts me in a bad mood.
